question: Under MCL 339.2502a(1), what is the minimum age the department may issue a real estate license to?
explanation: The department shall not issue a license to an individual who is under the age of 18 years.

question: Under MCL 339.2502a(7), how long must an individual whose license was revoked wait before applying for a new license?
choice_b: At least 3 years after service of the final revocation order
explanation: An individual whose license is revoked shall not apply for a new license for at least 3 years after service of the final order of revocation, and shall not receive credit for prior education, experience, or exams.

question: Per MCL 339.2502a(7), if a revoked licensee later reapplies, what happens to any examinations they passed before the revocation?
choice_a: They remain valid and count toward the new application
choice_b: Only the most recent exam score counts
choice_c: The applicant does not receive credit for examinations passed before the revocation
choice_d: The department automatically waives the exam requirement
explanation: The applicant shall not receive credit for education or experience acquired, or examinations passed, before the revocation.

question: Under MCL 339.2502a(6), a real estate salesperson whose license lapsed may be relicensed without a new exam within 3 years of expiration if they submit proof of which of the following?
choice_a: Only a signed letter of good standing from a former broker
choice_b: Payment of the late fee alone, with no education or exam requirement
choice_c: A notarized affidavit of continued competence
choice_d: 6 clock hours of CE per elapsed year, OR 40 clock hours of prelicensure courses in the preceding 12 months, OR passing the salesperson exam
explanation: The individual must submit proof meeting one of three paths: continuing education hours proportional to elapsed years, 40 clock hours of prelicensure courses in the preceding 12 months, or passing the salesperson exam -- plus paying the applicable fees.

question: Per MCL 339.2502b(1), engaging in more than how many real estate sales in any 12-month period is considered 'engaging in the sale of real estate as a principal vocation,' triggering the broker license requirement for an owner-seller?
explanation: Engaging in more than 5 real estate sales in any 12-month period is one of the defined ways an owner is considered engaged in the sale of real estate as a principal vocation.

question: Under MCL 339.2502b(1)(c), devoting more than what proportion of working time, or more than how many hours per week in any 6-month period, to selling real estate makes an owner's activity a 'principal vocation'?
choice_a: Over 25% of working time, or more than 10 hours per week
choice_b: Over 50% of working time, or more than 15 hours per week
choice_c: Over 75% of working time, or more than 20 hours per week
choice_d: Any amount of time at all
explanation: Devoting over 50% of working time, or more than 15 hours per week in any 6-month period, to the sale of real estate is one of the defined principal-vocation thresholds.

question: Per MCL 339.2502b(3), if a licensee is selling property they own or have an interest in, when must they disclose their ownership and licensure to the purchaser in writing?
choice_c: Before an offer to purchase is signed
choice_d: Disclosure is not required if the licensee is also the listing agent
explanation: The licensee shall reveal the facts of ownership or interest and their licensure to the purchaser, in writing, before an offer to purchase is signed.

question: Under MCL 339.2503(1), the license exemption for a person selling a never-before-occupied detached single-family dwelling they built applies only if the person built it while licensed under which article?
choice_a: No prior licensure is required for this exemption
explanation: This exemption applies to a person that sells such a dwelling that was built by the person while licensed under article 24.

question: Per MCL 339.2503(2), is an attorney-at-law rendering services as an attorney-at-law subject to Article 25's licensing requirements?
choice_a: No, Article 25 does not apply to an attorney-at-law rendering services as an attorney-at-law
choice_c: Only if the attorney charges a commission
explanation: Article 25 does not apply to an attorney-at-law who is rendering services as an attorney-at-law.

question: Under MCL 339.2504(1)(b)(i), of the 90 clock hours of prelicensure classroom courses required for a broker's license, how many hours minimum must be instruction on civil rights law and fair housing law?
explanation: At least 9 clock hours of the broker's 90-hour prelicensure requirement must be instruction on civil rights law and fair housing law.

question: Per MCL 339.2504(1)(b)(ii), are the 90 hours of broker prelicensure instruction in addition to, or inclusive of, the hours required for a salesperson's license?
choice_a: They replace the salesperson hours entirely
choice_b: Inclusive of the salesperson hours -- no additional hours needed
choice_c: In addition to the salesperson hours
choice_d: The statute does not address this
explanation: The 90 hours required for a broker's license are in addition to the hours required to obtain a real estate salesperson's license.

question: Under MCL 339.2504(2), before taking the real estate salesperson's examination, an applicant must complete at least how many clock hours of approved prelicensure classroom courses in principles of real estate?
explanation: An applicant must show proof of successfully completing at least 40 clock hours of approved prelicensure classroom courses in principles of real estate.

question: Per MCL 339.2504(2), of the salesperson's 40-hour prelicensure requirement, how many clock hours minimum must cover civil rights law and equal opportunity in housing?
explanation: The 40-hour salesperson prelicensure requirement must include at least 4 clock hours of instruction on civil rights law and equal opportunity in housing.

question: Under MCL 339.2504(2), an applicant must complete their 40 hours of salesperson prelicensure education within what period preceding the date of application?
explanation: The applicant must complete the 40 hours of prelicensure education within the 36-month period preceding the date of the application.

question: Per MCL 339.2504(1)(d), which single credential may the department by rule recognize as equivalent to completing broker prelicensure classroom courses?
choice_a: A high school diploma with 5 years of sales experience
choice_b: An associate degree in any field
choice_d: A real estate salesperson license alone, regardless of duration
explanation: The department may determine that possession of a law degree (among other listed credentials, such as a bachelor's or master's degree in business or finance) is equivalent to completing the prelicensure classroom courses.

question: Under MCL 339.2504(3)(b), an approved prelicensure course must cover one or more listed topics. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The law of agency is one of the topics an approved prelicensure course must cover, along with license law, property law, tax law, conveyances, financing, appraisal, design/construction, marketing, and sales/office management.

question: Per MCL 339.2504(4), a prelicensure course must be designed to be taught for at least how long, not including breaks, meals, or unrelated activities?
explanation: A course shall be designed to be taught for at least 1 clock hour, not including time spent on breaks, meals, or other unrelated activities.

question: Under MCL 339.2504(4), which of the following entities may conduct an approved prelicensure course?
choice_a: Any private tutor with a real estate license
choice_d: A licensed real estate brokerage with no other approval
explanation: A local public school district is one of the listed entities (along with community colleges, degree-granting institutions of higher education, and other department-approved providers) that may conduct an approved prelicensure course.

question: Per MCL 339.2504a(1)(b), in each license cycle before the department's new rule-based hour count takes effect, how many clock hours of continuing education must a licensee complete?
explanation: In each license cycle before the department's new rule takes effect, a licensee must complete 18 clock hours of eligible continuing education courses.

question: Under MCL 339.2504a(2)(a), of the required annual continuing education hours, how many hours minimum must involve laws, rules, and court cases regarding real estate?
explanation: A licensee must complete not less than 2 hours per year of courses that involve laws, rules, and court cases regarding real estate.

question: Per MCL 339.2504a(2)(a), of the required annual continuing education hours, how many hours minimum must involve compliance with fair housing laws?
choice_d: Fair housing compliance hours are not separately required
explanation: A licensee must complete not less than 1 hour per year of courses involving compliance with local, state, or federal fair housing laws.

question: Under MCL 339.2504a(2)(c), to confirm identity at a continuing education course, a licensee must present their pocket card (or license ID number) plus what second item?
choice_b: A government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license
choice_c: A signed statement from their broker
explanation: The licensee must present an operator's or chauffeur's license, a state personal ID card, or other government-issued photo identification to the course provider.

question: Per MCL 339.2504a(2)(e), if a licensee repeats an eligible continuing education course they already completed, do they earn additional CE hours?
choice_a: Yes, hours accumulate each time the course is taken
choice_b: Yes, but only up to double the original hours
choice_c: No, the licensee does not earn additional hours for repeating a course
choice_d: Only if a different instructor teaches it the second time
explanation: If a licensee successfully completes an eligible CE course, the licensee does not earn additional hours toward the requirements if the licensee repeats that course.

question: Under MCL 339.2504a(3), how long must a licensee retain evidence of meeting their continuing education requirements after certifying compliance?
explanation: A licensee shall retain acceptable evidence demonstrating the CE requirements were met for not less than 4 years after the date of certification.

question: Per MCL 339.2505(2), the department shall not issue a real estate broker's license to an individual convicted of what?
choice_c: Any crime whatsoever, with no exceptions
choice_d: Failure to file taxes on time
explanation: The department shall not issue a real estate broker's license to an individual who has been convicted of embezzlement or misappropriation of funds.

question: Under MCL 339.2505(3), if a broker's branch office is located more than how many miles from the nearest boundary of the municipality where the main office sits, must an associate broker directly supervise the branch?
explanation: If a branch office is located more than 25 miles from the nearest boundary of the municipality in which the main office is located, the broker shall ensure the branch office is under the direct supervision of an associate broker.

question: Per MCL 339.2505(3), what does 'direct supervision' of a branch office mean under this section?
choice_a: An associate broker reviews branch records once per year
choice_b: The main office broker calls the branch daily
choice_c: An associate broker is physically present at the branch office on a regular basis to supervise and manage business during ordinary business hours
choice_d: A salesperson is designated as acting supervisor
explanation: Direct supervision means an associate broker is physically present at the branch office on a regular basis to supervise and manage the business during ordinary business hours.

question: Under MCL 339.2505(6)(b), a passing score on an examination (or a portion of one given in separate parts) is valid for how long from the date of the exam?
explanation: A passing score on an examination, or on a portion of an examination given in separate parts, is valid for 1 year from the date of the examination.

question: Per MCL 339.2505(7), a broker license applicant must prove the equivalent of how many years of full-time real estate experience?
explanation: The department shall require proof of the equivalent of 3 years of full-time experience in the business of real estate.

question: Under MCL 339.2505(7)(b)(i), a real estate salesperson earns 1 year of experience credit toward the broker requirement for each 12-month period of licensure in which they closed how many or more real estate transactions?
explanation: A salesperson receives 1 year of credit for each 12-month period of licensure in which they closed 5 or more real estate transactions.

question: Per MCL 339.2506(1), an individual acting under this article must have their license and pocket card (or temporary license) on their person, or what alternative is acceptable?
choice_a: No alternative is acceptable; the physical card is always required
choice_b: A verbal statement that they are licensed
choice_c: A photocopy or digital image of that pocket card or temporary license
choice_d: A business card listing their license number
explanation: A licensee must have on their person their pocket card or temporary license, or a photocopy or digital image of that pocket card or temporary license.

question: Under MCL 339.2506(5), during a license transfer to a new broker, the department shall consider the pocket card proper evidence of licensing for how many days from the latest date on the back of the card?
explanation: The department shall consider the pocket card as proper evidence of licensing for 45 days from the latest date written on the back of the card.

question: Per MCL 339.2507(1), if a real estate salesperson is discharged or terminates employment, the broker must deliver or mail the salesperson's license to the department within how many days?
explanation: The real estate broker shall deliver or mail by certified mail to the department, within 5 days, the real estate salesperson's license.

question: Under MCL 339.2507(4), may the department issue more than one license to a real estate salesperson for the same period of time?
choice_a: Yes, up to two active licenses
choice_b: No, the department shall not issue more than 1 license to a salesperson for the same period
choice_c: Yes, if the salesperson works for two different brokers
choice_d: The statute does not address this
explanation: The department shall not issue more than 1 license to a real estate salesperson for the same period of time.

question: Per MCL 339.2508(1), a real estate broker's license may be issued to which of the following?
choice_c: An individual, sole proprietorship, partnership, association, corporation, LLC, common law trust, or a combination of those entities
choice_d: Only a partnership of at least two individuals
explanation: The department may issue a real estate broker's license to an individual, sole proprietorship, partnership, association, corporation, LLC, common law trust, or a combination of those entities.

question: Under MCL 339.2508(3), what happens to the associate real estate broker's license of a principal who ceases to be connected with the licensed entity?
choice_b: Nothing changes until the next renewal cycle
choice_c: It converts to a salesperson license
explanation: The associate real estate broker's license of a principal who ceases to be connected with the entity is suspended automatically.

question: Per MCL 339.2508(5), if a real estate broker's license is revoked, what happens to the licenses of the salespersons employed by that broker?
choice_a: They are automatically suspended, pending a change of employer and issuance of a new license
choice_c: They are permanently revoked as well
choice_d: They convert automatically to independent broker licenses
explanation: If a broker's license is revoked, the licenses of all salespersons employed by the broker and all affiliated associate brokers are automatically suspended, pending a change of employer and issuance of a new license.

question: Under MCL 339.2509(2), may an individual hold more than one associate real estate broker's license as a nonprincipal?
choice_b: No -- an individual shall not hold more than 1 associate broker's license as a nonprincipal, though they may hold multiple as a principal
choice_d: No, associate broker licenses as a nonprincipal are never permitted
explanation: An individual shall not hold more than 1 associate real estate broker's license as a nonprincipal, but may hold 1 or more associate broker's licenses as a principal.

question: Per MCL 339.2513, if the department requires a bond as a condition of licensure after a denial, suspension, or revocation, what is the maximum sum for a cash deposit in lieu of a bond?
explanation: The department may require a bond for a period not to exceed 5 years, or cash in a sum fixed by the department not to exceed $5,000.00.

question: Under MCL 339.2513, for how many years at most may the department require a licensure bond to remain on file?
explanation: The bond may be required for a period not to exceed 5 years, issued by an admitted surety insurer.

question: Per MCL 339.2514, a nonresident applicant for a broker or salesperson license must file what kind of consent regarding legal actions in Michigan?
choice_a: An irrevocable consent that actions may be commenced against them via service of process on the department
choice_b: No special consent is required of nonresidents
choice_c: A consent limited to actions filed within 90 days of licensure
choice_d: A waiver of all legal rights in Michigan
explanation: A nonresident applicant shall file an irrevocable consent that an action may be commenced against them by service of process on the department, valid and binding as if served directly on the applicant.

question: Under MCL 339.2516a, during normal business hours, a licensee must allow an authorized department representative to do what?
choice_a: Only review records if a warrant is presented
choice_b: Enter places of business and inspect documents/records reasonably necessary for an investigation or review
choice_c: Access records only with 30 days' advance notice
choice_d: Nothing; department inspections require a court order
explanation: A licensee shall allow any authorized representative of the department to enter places of business in Michigan and inspect any document or record reasonably necessary for an investigation, business review, or administration of the article.
